f.title: Trials of registered products in the registered indication report under Procedure 6
f.statement: For a study of a registered drug in its registered indication (post-marketing), safety reports go to the Risk Management and Drug Information Department under Procedure 6; for a registered medical device, to the Medical Devices Division.
f.legal_basis: MoH Procedure 164/01 (this Q&A is binding as part of it)

f.title: Registered comparator: report per Procedure 6 if the sponsor is the MAH, otherwise to the Clinical Trials Department stating whether the MAH was told
f.statement: For a registered product used as comparator: a sponsor who is the registration holder follows Procedure 6 (drug) or the device division; an investigator-sponsor reports to the registration holder; any other sponsor sends the report to the Clinical Trials Department, stating whether the registration holder was notified.
f.legal_basis: MoH Procedure 164/01 (this Q&A is binding as part of it)

rows.quote_en: 1.1.2 How to report in a study of a registered product for a registered indication used as a comparator? Answer: a) where the sponsor is the registration holder, it must act according to Procedure 6 and report to the Risk Management and Drug Information Department (drug) or the Medical Devices Division (device). b) Where the trial sponsor is an investigator, it is his responsibility to report to the registration holder (sections 5.1.2.2, 5.1.3.2 and 5.1.4.2). c) Where the trial sponsor is not the registration holder, the sponsor shall send the report to the Clinical Trials Department. When reporting to the Clinical Trials Department, it must be added whether notice was passed to the registration holder.

f.title: Report a SUSAR only when the company assesses it as related and unexpected per the RSI; document the investigator's view
f.statement: A SUSAR is reported when the company assesses the SAE as related to the investigational product or study procedure and unexpected per the RSI. The company must document the investigator's opinion, but reporting follows the company's causality assessment; reportable categories are "related" or "reasonable possibility" (certain/definite, probable/likely, possible; WHO causality criteria may help).
f.legal_basis: MoH Procedure 164/01 (this Q&A is binding as part of it)

rows.quote_en: 2.1 Should a SUSAR be reported only when the company assesses that there is a relationship? Answer: Yes. Report when the SAE is related, according to the company's assessment, to the investigational product or the study procedure and is unexpected based on the RSI. The company is responsible for documenting the investigator's opinion, but further reporting will be based only on the company's causality assessment. The categories requiring reporting are: 'related' or 'reasonable possibility of a relationship' (certain/definite, probable/likely, possible – the [WHO causality assessment document] may be used).

f.statement: DSMB conclusions that change nothing are not reported; conclusions deciding protocol changes affecting patient safety or stopping the trial are sent to the mailbox of the unit that handled the application.

rows.quote_en: 4.1 Is there an obligation to transfer reports in investigator-initiated studies where the investigator is also the sponsor? Answer: the investigator takes responsibility for such a study also as sponsor and is therefore obliged to report according to Ministry of Health instructions (Procedures 14 and 164). Where the trial sponsor is an investigator, it is his responsibility to report to the registration holder (sections 5.1.2.2, 5.1.3.2 and 5.1.4.2). The investigator is responsible for periodically updating the trial documents also on the investigational product (new publications in the literature, update of the physician leaflet, etc.).

f.title: Compassionate use: drugs follow risk management (solicited) rules; ATIMPs and devices to the Clinical Trials Department
f.statement: For urgent and compassionate treatments, drugs follow the Risk Management and Drug Information Department instructions (solicited reports); advanced therapies (ATIMP) and medical devices are reported to the Clinical Trials Department.
